title: Police cleared in fatal shooting of man at Scarborough apartment building
article: The Special Investigations Unit has concluded that a Toronto police officer was justified in using lethal force on a knife-wielding man in Scarborough last month.
Malcolm Jackman, 39, was fatally shot by police after holding a knife to the throat of a hostage outside an apartment building at 140 Adanac Dr. on the evening of June 8.
The SIU interviewed the subject officer, five witness officers and 10 civilian witnesses as part of the investigation.
The investigation revealed that two officers were dispatched to an apartment at 140 Adanac to assist paramedics with an emotionally disturbed person.

While on scene, a man told one of the officers that Jackman attacked him with a knife at a bus stop. Though this wasn't why police were originally called to the building, they went to investigate and found Jackman talking to himself in the building stairwell. Armed with a knife, Jackman asked the officers to shoot him.
One officer discharged pepper spray but that had no effect.
Jackman then left the building through the stairwell exit door and took a hostage.

"Both officers commanded Mr. Jackman to drop the knife multiple times while pointing their firearms at him," the SIU said in a news release. "The subject officer observed Mr. Jackman moving the knife closer to his hostage's neck and discharged her firearm four times in his direction."
Jackman was taken to Sunnybrook hospital where he died.
The SIU investigates whenever there is a serious injury or death involving police.
